title: Duke as accompanist
summary: Cootie played better with Duke than any pianist, because Duke felt every move and left nothing open.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. What -- you know, from the point of view of two piano players, I mean, it wasn't quite the same thing to be playing with Stray as it would be to be playing with Duke back of you, was it?
Oh, no.
Tell me what the difference was.
Well, there was a world of difference. Duke was the greatest piano player that I ever played with.
How come?
Well, he could feel you. You know, how to back you up.
Yeah.
He could feel every movement that you was going to make.
Yeah.
You know, and you were more comfortable playing with him, which I was, than any other piano player I ever played with.
No kidding.
Yeah.
Well, it would seem to me that the reason -- one of the reasons was that Duke, his instrument was the band,
so his instrument wasn't really the piano. So when he's playing piano, he's working for the band.
Yeah.
He's helping his band. He's helping every guy in his band.
Yeah.
Because his band is his instrument.
Yeah.

So he's working for himself at the same time as he's working for you. Whereas the average piano player, his instrument is piano, so he's himself all the time, even though he's accompanying you. He's still himself. Which is not quite the same thing. Do you follow me? When Duke's accompanying you, he's 100 percent accompanying you. He's not proving himself on the piano at all, is he?
No. I don't know. Maybe because I played with him so many years, and he knew me. This is my feeling.
Yeah.
And this is the feeling that I used to get from Duke. And I could play better with him than I could with any other piano player.
Yeah. Yeah.
Maybe because I, you know, I worked with him so long. And he didn't leave anything open. He made
you feel comfortable blowing playing all the time.
Yeah. You weren't worried you had to fill something in.
Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. You were doing your picture and he was putting the frame in everywhere.
Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. And Strayhorn wouldn't approach it from that angle, really, would he? I mean, he would just be playing --
He'd just be playing, yeah.
-- something that he felt was beautiful.
Yeah.
And playing for himself, as well as for you at the same time.
Yeah.
